title: The Glass-Bottom Boathouse
logline: The Captain hires Ted to design a boathouse and judges every choice in sailing metaphors nobody can decode, so Lily, his art consultant, starts 'translating' both men, and Ted's boathouse grows a coral reef, eleven hatches and a helipad. Meanwhile Robin trains Marshall in the Captain's unblinking stare and Barney adopts 'Stepping off!' as his exit line, and both come in handy at the unveiling.
coldOpen: Kids, in 2012 I landed the biggest commission of my career. It became the smallest building I ever designed. Blame the client, who only spoke in sailing metaphors, and your Aunt Lily, who swore she could translate.

guests.name: Thornton Pike
guests.role: CEO of Pike Paints, a stone-faced corporate witness with a combover who has outlasted seven lawyers and cannot survive four seconds of silence

scenes.summary: Mosbius Designs. Lily swears she speaks fluent Captain. The Captain reviews Ted's glass dream boathouse in sailing metaphors; Lily translates them as 'sail-ier', 'a coral reef' and 'more hatches', and translates Ted's architect-speak back as 'he'll trim the jib'. Captain steps off; Ted is thrilled. Freeze: Lily has understood exactly one thing the Captain ever said.

beats.line: Mosbius Designs. One architect, one client, and one very confident art consultant.
Lily, is it true the Captain fired his last architect without saying a word?
That's a lie. He said one word.
What word?
Starboard. Nobody's seen the guy since.
Lily, I can't blow this. Since I was nine, I've wanted to hang a building out over the water.
I know, Ted. You said so in your toast at my wedding.
Relax. Three years as his art consultant. I speak fluent Captain.
Mister Mosby.
Captain! Welcome to Mosbius Designs. Can I get you anything? Coffee? Sparkling water?
Sparkling water is for people who are afraid of the sea.
Then let's dive in. The Mosby Boathouse. Glass and steel, cantilevered thirty feet out over Long Island Sound.
She's a lot of sail for so little keel.
Is that good?
That's great! Sails are the good part. He wants it sail-ier.
Sail-ier. I love that. A roof shaped like a sail. One giant triangle of glass.
Mister Mosby. A man who reefs early never loses his mast.
Lily?
He wants a reef.
Like a coral reef?
Under a glass floor. With fish. So many fish.
Bold. Then the cantilever becomes a dialogue between the tectonics of the shore and the vernacular of the sea.
Mrs. Aldrin?
He says he'll trim the jib.
Good man.
Batten down the hatches, Mister Mosby. The tide waits for no man.
More hatches.
The unveiling is Saturday, at the yacht club. Stepping off!
He loves it! A sail roof, a coral reef, and more hatches!
Lily, that's the most specific feedback a client has ever given me.
Told you. Fluent.
I have to go. I need a book about hatches.
Kids, in three years, Lily had understood exactly one thing the Captain ever said. Stepping off. And only because he always left.

scenes.summary: Barney adopts 'Stepping off!' as the perfect exit line, then has to abandon a forty-dollar scotch to honor it. Marshall wants the Captain's stare for Thursday's deposition; Robin, veteran of nine-hour duck blinds, will coach him. Robin wants into the yacht club for its 1962 scotch. Ted steps out; Lily confesses she doesn't speak Captain (flashback: three years of 'aye'). Ted returns with the Captain's text, and Lily digs deeper: two decks.

beats.line: And then he said stepping off, and just left. No goodbye. No handshake.
He announced that he was leaving. And then he left.
Yeah?
Ted, that is the greatest exit line in the history of exits.
You drop your best line, you say stepping off, you're gone. She never sees you bomb on the second line.
Barney, you don't have a second line.
And now nobody will ever find out.
Forget the exit. Ted, did he really not blink? The whole meeting?
He doesn't blink. I once watched him stare down a seagull. The seagull moved to New Jersey.
Lily, I need that stare. Thursday I'm deposing Thornton Pike.
CEO of Pike Paints. Seven lawyers have tried to crack him. He's a vault with a combover.
Marshall, you can't do the stare. You cry at sunsets.
Because it's the sky saying goodbye, Robin!
Fine. I'll train you. Every winter, my dad put me in a duck blind for nine hours.
And if you blinked?
You were the decoy.
Ted. Is this unveiling at the Port Washington Yacht Club?
Yeah, why?
They have a 1962 Macallan they only pour for members and their guests. Congratulations. I'm your guest.
Watch and learn. Stepping off!
He just ordered a forty-dollar scotch.
I left a forty-dollar scotch.
You stepped off.
I did step off.
Rules are rules.
I'm going to call an aquarium. Lily, you're a genius.
I don't speak Captain.
What? Lily, you've worked for him for three years!
And for three years, I've said one word.
Mrs. Aldrin. Art is the wind. You cannot see her, but a wise man trims for her. Agreed?
Aye.
You're hired.
Now. Do we hang the Rothko to port, or abaft the beam?
Aye.
Both. Bold.
Lily, you told Ted the man wants a coral reef!
He said reef! It's not my fault he talks like a fortune cookie on a boat!
You have to tell Ted.
Marshall, I love this job. It's the only job I've ever had where nobody throws up on me.
Guys! The Captain texted.

messages.text: All hands on deck Saturday. Bring your crew.

beats.line: Lily. All hands on deck. Does that mean he wants a deck?
Two decks.

scenes.summary: Robin's stare boot camp. Marshall's deposition (flashback): he said nothing and Thornton Pike confessed to everything, so the stare is really about shutting up. Barney said stepping off on the Staten Island Ferry. Ted's boathouse now has a helipad. Lily comes to confess; Ted's speech about clients always cutting his best ideas shuts her up. Marshall tells her to tell him; Lily stares, and Marshall cracks instead.

beats.line: By Friday, the Mosby Boathouse had a sail roof, a coral reef, eleven hatches and two decks. It was perfect.
Don't blink.
Robin, my eyes are so dry I can hear them.
That's hour one in the blind.
I blinked! I blinked!
Decoy.
Marshall, how did the deposition go? Did the stare work?
Ted, it was beautiful. I stared at Thornton Pike for four whole minutes.
Are you going to ask me a question?
Is that a tear?
It's the wind.
Fine! We dumped forty barrels of paint in the Gowanus Canal!
And I cheated at my son's pinewood derby! The car had a motor!
Keep going.
I have never seen Casablanca! I just nod when people quote it!
I never said a word. Turns out the stare isn't about the eyes.
It's about shutting up.
People will say anything to fill a silence. Even the truth.
Word of advice. Never say stepping off on the Staten Island Ferry.
You didn't.
A Stinson honors his exit line, Marshall.
Barney, the ferry was in the middle of the harbor.
I'm aware of where it was, Robin.
Dad. Did Uncle Barney actually jump off the Staten Island Ferry?
He told the Coast Guard he slipped. He told us he stepped.
Guys, it's done. Sail roof, coral reef, eleven hatches, two decks. And a helipad.
Ted, that's not a boathouse. That's a cruise ship that gave up.
Why a helipad?
He texted come about. Lily says that means helipad.
Ted. I need to tell you something about the Captain.
Wait. Me first.
Every building I've ever designed, the client made me cut the best part. The spire. The gargoyles. The moat.
There was a moat?
It was a dentist's office.
This is the first client who keeps asking for more. Lily, do you know what that feels like?
Aye.
Big day tomorrow. I'm going to go sleep next to the model.
Lily. Tell him.
I ate the rest of your birthday cake! Standing up! In the dark!
Huh. It works on everybody.

scenes.summary: The Port Washington Yacht Club. Ted unveils his maximal boathouse; the Captain's metaphor breaks Lily, who confesses three years of 'aye'. Ted starts rambling; Marshall tells him to stop talking and do the stare. In the silence, the Captain speaks plainly: the boat is an eleven-foot dinghy his father built. Ted scraps his dream for a cedar shed with one west window. The Captain liked the reef. The Captain knew about Lily all along. 'Stepping off' was his father's line; Barney learns how his father used it.

beats.line: The Port Washington Yacht Club. Founded 1891. Last blinked in 1904.
This scotch is older than my father. And kinder.
I've been staring down the Captain since the bread basket. I blinked at the butter.
Decoy.
Captain. The Mosby Boathouse. Sail roof. Eleven hatches. Two decks. A helipad.
And under a glass floor, a living coral reef.
Mister Mosby. You've hung a ship's bell on a duck.
Lily?
He loves ducks. Add ducks.
Mrs. Aldrin. What did I just say?
Aye?
Okay! I don't speak Captain! For three years I've just been saying aye!
The reef?
He said reef! I panicked!
The hatches? The decks? The helipad?
I panicked a lot, Ted.
Captain, I'm so sorry. I can start over. Stone, timber, a postmodern deconstruction of the vernacular—
Ted. Stop talking.
The stare isn't a threat, buddy. He's waiting. Nobody ever stops talking long enough.
She's eleven feet long.
The boat is eleven feet long?
Little Georgie. My father built her the summer I turned eight.
Ted. The reef is bigger than the boat.
We sailed her every evening. Then I grew up and bought bigger boats. Then bigger ones.
She's been under a tarp for forty years. Little boats get lonely in big harbors, Mister Mosby.
So much sail for so little keel. You never wanted a monument. You wanted somewhere small enough for her to come home to.
Aye.
I know that one!
Then forget the Mosby Boathouse. A cedar shed. One window facing west, for the sunset. One bench, wide enough for two.
Ted. You've wanted to hang a building over the water since you were nine.
I know. But it's not my boat.
And the coral reef?
Gone.
Pity. I liked the reef.
Mrs. Aldrin. I've known since your first day.
You knew? Then why did you keep me?
Everyone else asks me to explain myself. You just agree. It's very restful.
Stepping off!
Sir, wait. Where does that even come from?
My father said it every evening, stepping off Little Georgie onto the dock.
Oh no. I've been using your father's sacred words to leave women's apartments.
So did he.
I came here for a scotch. I'm leaving with feelings.
Kids, the day Little Georgie came home, the Captain didn't cry, of course. But he blinked. Once. For the Captain, that's sobbing.
